turns.text: Why did researchers need Locally Linear Embedding, and where were the existing methods getting stuck?

Sam Roweis and Lawrence Saul introduced locally linear embedding as a nonlinear dimensionality-reduction algorithm that preserves local reconstruction weights. Instead of modeling global distances directly, LLE keeps each point locally reconstructable from its neighbors.
Each point is reconstructed from neighbors, and the low-dimensional map preserves those weights.

Experts generally treat LLE as a key manifold-learning method complementary to Isomap. Its long-term legacy is the idea that preserving local reconstruction relations can reveal nonlinear structure without an explicit global model.
The thread continues with t-SNE, where researchers push the problem one step further.
